thread_text:
riley (contractor): Hey team — I'm converting from contractor to full-time on 2026-11-05. Quick Q: will my PTO be prorated for November? Also there's a product freeze Nov 20-Dec 5 (performance prep) — can I use PTO during that window if needed?

anna: @sam any guidance? Riley's start/offer is signed but payroll hasn't run the conversion yet.

sam (People Ops): Congrats on the conversion! Short answers: yes, we will prorate the first month's accrual based on your official start date; and there is a limited blackout during the review prep window where PTO requires manager approval due to staffing constraints.

sam (People Ops): Details: 1) Contractors do not accrue PTO while on contractor agreements. On conversion to FT, we create an entitlement starting on your FT start date. 2) Proration: monthly accrual * (days employed in month / total days in month). We record a prorated credit in the HR portal on your first payroll run. 3) Usage guardrails: new hires receive the prorated accrual immediately, but requests for more than 3 consecutive business days within the first 30 days require manager + People Ops sign-off.

sam (People Ops): Example calc (inline): `monthly_accrual = 8 hrs; start = 2026-11-05; days_in_nov = 30; days_employed = 26; prorated = 8 * (26/30) = 6.93 hrs` — we round to nearest 0.25 hour in the system.

managers: If you need to approve an exception (e.g., >3 days in month 1), email people-ops@redwood with subject `Conversion PTO Exception` and include employee ID + dates + business rationale.

jess (Recruiting): For payroll: please confirm the employee ID so we can avoid delays. I attached the signed offer to the conversion ticket.

sam (People Ops): Thanks @jess. Process steps for the team: 1) Recruiting confirms signed offer and start date on the HR ticket. 2) Manager confirms start on the People Ops ticket. 3) People Ops issues prorated credit (code CONV-PRORATE) and updates HR portal entitlement. 4) Payroll posts on next cycle.

payroll-bot: Note: CONV-PRORATE adjustments are typically posted within one payroll cycle after People Ops updates the record. Use timesheet code PTO for time off entries. Link to conversion checklist: https://hr.redwood.example/conversion-checklist

matt: About the Nov20-Dec5 window  do we have a formal blackout or is it soft (manager discretion)?

sam (People Ops): It's a soft blackout: we ask teams to limit PTO unless coverage is arranged. Any PTO in that window should include a coverage note in the HR portal. Critical roles may be blocked; managers will be notified if their direct reports are impacted.

riley (contractor): Appreciate the clarity. One more: if I had unpaid time off during my contractor period, does that factor into the proration?

sam (People Ops): No, unpaid contractor days don't count toward FT accrual history. Proration only uses the FT start date. If you worked >40 hours as contractor in the prior week and we agreed to front-load a comp credit, manager must attach that approval and People Ops will evaluate case-by-case.

anna: I'll email people-ops@redwood with Riley's employee ID and the signed offer now. Thanks everyone.

riley (contractor): Thanks! I'll plan my week off request after the entitlements show up. :thumbsup:
